newsitem.title: GERMANY: Weakness overcomes Bunds, futures in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Weakness overcomes Bunds, futures in late trade.

text.p: German Bunds and futures surrendered to weakness in late trade, failing to find buyers despite 10-year cash yields trading over 6.00 percent for most of the day.
Traders said activity was subdued in the second half of the session after stronger than expected February industrial production data toppled bond prices in early trade.
By 1612 GMT, the DTB June Bund future was trading 29 basis points lower at 99.16, holding just off its daily low of 99.06.
"The cash market was very boring today," said one bonds trader in Frankfurt. "We have seen very little trade."
The 10-year cash Bund was trading at 99.70 by 1617 GMT for a yield of 6.039 percent.

"The Bund market has clearly been following the U.S. for the last few days -- the Bund/Treasury spread has remained fairly stable," said John Butler, fixed income analyst at WestLB Research in Duesseldorf.
"But today we did get the first significant piece of German fundamental news in a little while with industrial production."
Industrial production leapt to 1.9 percent in February after a fall of 1.7 percent in January.
The numbers took the market -- which had been expecting a 0.8 percent rise on the month -- by surprise, and sent Bund futures tumbling through key support in the 99.28 region.
"The number was a bit higher than had been expected and as a result it did hit the market a bit harder," said Butler.
The Frankfurt based bonds trader said that if 99.05 and 99.00 support levels came under pressure, the contract could be heading towards 98.50 in the next few sessions.
Upside potential would be limited to the 99.60 area.
"But it's all hanging on tomorrow's U.S. figures," the trader said. "That's the most important figure this week."
Economists polled by Reuters are forecasting that 182,000 jobs will have been added to the non-farm payrolls in March, versus 339,000 in February.

But analysts said world bond markets should be reasonably resistant to any surprise from the employment report. "Markets are convinced the Fed is on course to raise rates, so even if the number comes in significantly more or less strongly than expected, it shouldn't change those fears," said Butler.
The 10-year T-note/Bund yield spread stood at 95 basis points at 1643 GMT, reflecting Bunds' poor performance aginst the U.S. market.
